        16                  SENATOR LIBOUS:    Thank you,

        17       Mr. President.

        18                  I rise to second the nomination of

        19       Barry Kluger as the inspector general for the

        20       MTA.

        21                  I am very pleased that Governor

        22       Spitzer has sent us a candidate with these

        23       outstanding qualifications.  Spending time

        24       with Mr. Kluger and having a number of

        25       conversations with him to get a feel for his

         1       qualifications for the job, I came away

         2       extremely confident, as the committee did when

         3       it met and had questions for him and reviewed

         4       his qualifications.

         5                  Mr. Kluger himself is a daily rider

         6       of the MTA, so he understands his role as an

         7       advocate, as the inspector general.  He also

         8       has a very, very strong desire to work with us

         9       here in the Legislature and other colleagues

        10       throughout various transportation agencies.

        11                  His background, an investigation

        12       background with the Bronx County district

        13       attorney's office, I think gives him the

        14       qualifications that we need in this very, very

        15       important role as inspector general.

        16                  And, Mr. President, I am quite

        17       confident that he will be an outstanding

        18       inspector general, that Governor Spitzer has

        19       sent us a very well qualified candidate.  And

        20       it is a pleasure for me to second his

        21       nomination.

         1                  I too want to rise to second the

         2       nomination of Mr. Kluger to be the inspector

         3       general of the MTA.  It's a very important

         4       position, the MTA having billions of dollars

         5       in operating and capital money go through its

         6       doors.  And over the years we've seen a lot of

         7       that money, its efficacy, called into

         8       question.

         9                  I think Mr. Kluger and his

        10       background in law enforcement, his extensive

        11       experience at the Bronx district attorney's

        12       office and in other places, will go a long way

        13       to making sure that the dollars spent by the

        14       MTA are spent effectively and honestly and in

        15       the public's interest.

        16                  In addition, one of the most

        17       important aspects I think that he brings to

        18       this job is that being in a criminal law

        19       enforcement background, with the MTA now the

        20       recipient of large amounts of federal money

        21       for antiterrorism, that we can be sure that

        22       when we wake up in the morning we won't see,

        23       or hopefully won't see, if I'm confident in

        24       his abilities, that that money won't be wasted

        25       or frittered away but will be used to protect

         1       New Yorkers as they ride the system, as they

         2       go on our bridges and tunnels, as they ride

         3       the commuter railways.

         4                  So I'm pretty confident that Barry

         5       Kluger is the right man for the job.  I

         6       applaud the Governor for his appointment and

         7       look forward to working with him in the

         8       future.

         9                  Thank you, Mr. President.

        17                  I also rise to second the

        18       nomination of Barry Kluger to be the inspector

        19       general of the MTA.

        20                  Mr. Kluger is both a constituent

        21       and a neighbor from New York City, and I have

        22       had many opportunities to chat with him

        24       the importance of public service and the work

         1       people of New York.  And I've also had a

         2       chance to meet with him to discuss his new

         3       mission and his new agenda at the MTA.

         4                  And I share my colleagues' support

         5       for his talents and skills and commitment to

         6       taking on this very large job to make sure

         7       that the MTA is run as we need it to be run,

         8       that the funds are accounted for, that there

         9       are audits both from a financial perspective

        10       and from the perspective of programmatic

        11       operations.

        12                  And any authority and any

        13       government agency needs to have the ability to

        14       technically self-police and keep itself both

        15       honest and transparent.  And so I am delighted

        16       that a man of Mr. Kluger's caliber is willing

        17       to shift gears in his career and move from his

        18       work at the district attorney's office to

        19       taking on this enormous responsibility for the

        20       MTA and in fact for all of the people in

        21       New York State.

        22                  So I congratulate him and look

        23       forward to continuing to work with him.

        24                  Thank you, Mr. President.
